clue.text: 1000 pounds paid for our incoming food expert

indicators.note: something incoming comes inside, so the possessive word is placed within the letters around it

blocks.note: G, a grand, is slang for a thousand pounds
to meet a bill is to pay it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone splashes a fortune on a lavish meal for a visiting food critic.
explanation.walkthrough: A grand is British slang for a thousand pounds, and paying for something is meeting its cost.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmet is a connoisseur of fine cooking and eating, someone with expert taste in dishes.

clue.text: Fumes a lot, as they talk too much

blocks.note: gas and fumes are both vapours
bags of something is plenty of it

explanation.surface: Someone seethes with irritation at chatterboxes who never stop.
explanation.walkthrough: Fumes looks like a verb of anger; here it is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasbags is informal for people who chatter endlessly, windbags or blabbermouths.

clue.text: Cool mud oven exploded

indicators.note: an exploded thing is blown apart, so its letters scatter and regroup

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clay oven blew up, which was rather cool.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay cool is to remain calm and unaffected by emotion, which is to be unmoved.

clue.text: Mercury left in contact with fruit

blocks.note: Mercury is this puzzle's setter, so the setter refers to themself
L is the abbreviation for left
on means touching, resting against

explanation.surface: The planet or the metal, left touching a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercury is the setter's pseudonym, so it stands for the setter: me.
explanation.definitionFit: A melon is a large juicy fruit of the gourd family, such as a cantaloupe.

clue.text: They feel it's time to have castle refurbished

indicators.note: a refurbished building is remodelled, so the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

blocks.note: ten o'clock is a time
taken as written

explanation.surface: Owners sense the moment has come to do up their castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They feel' reads as people's opinion, but the definition is literal: things that feel by touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tentacles are the flexible limbs an octopus or squid uses for touching and grasping.

clue.text: They're naughty when Carl's working outside

indicators.note: the name is put to work, i.e. rearranged into a new order
the rearranged letters sit on the outside, wrapping round the other word

blocks.note: the name with its possessive s, as letters
as and when are both conjunctions of time

explanation.surface: Children misbehave whenever Carl is out at work.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive s on the name is part of the fodder, and the rearranged name wraps the short word for when.
explanation.definitionFit: Rascals are mischievous scamps, so the plural noun describes people who behave badly.

clue.text: Companion to regret wearing ruffle

indicators.note: the companion is worn by the other word, so it sits inside it

blocks.note: to rue is to regret
CH is a Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A sorry partner sports a frilly collar.
explanation.walkthrough: RU(CH)E. The Companion of Honour is a British honour abbreviated CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruche is a gathered strip of fabric used as trimming, much like a ruffle or frill.

clue.text: Sudden increase cleaner accepted as an extra payment

indicators.note: the swell accepts the cleaner, taking it inside

blocks.note: a surge is a sudden rise
a char, or charwoman, is a cleaner

explanation.surface: A cleaner takes a sudden pay rise as a bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: SUR(CHAR)GE. Char is British for a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcharge is an additional fee added on top of the normal price.

clue.text: A good man behind a bag counter!

indicators.note: behind places the good man after the other pieces

blocks.note: the second a, taken as written
to bag something is to gain it
a saint, abbreviated ST, is a good man

explanation.surface: A decent fellow stands behind a shop counter selling bags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' is not a shop fixture but the preposition, as in counter to.
explanation.definitionFit: Counter to and against both mean in opposition to something.

clue.text: Postpone imprisoning us while away

indicators.note: imprisoning locks the pronoun inside the other word

blocks.note: to while away time is to spend it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Delay locking us up while someone is out of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'While away' looks like 'during an absence'; it is the verb phrase for passing time.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to defer or put it off for a time.

clue.text: Pass easily, taking year off before working

indicators.note: taking something off removes it, here the abbreviation for a year from the end

blocks.note: simply and easily both mean without difficulty
Y is the standard abbreviation for year
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Someone sails through a test after a gap year before starting a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass easily' reads as succeeding without trouble, but Pass is a noun: the Simplon is an Alpine pass between Switzerland and Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Simplon is a mountain route through the Alps linking Switzerland with Italy.

clue.text: Engineer's going without proper food

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go round the other word

blocks.note: CE is a civil engineer, plus the possessive s
real and proper both mean genuine

explanation.surface: An engineer goes hungry, missing out on decent meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is read in its archaic sense of outside: CE(REAL)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereals are grain foods such as breakfast flakes, oats and wheat products eaten daily.

clue.text: Service commercial vehicle, say, at back

indicators.note: going back means the last two pieces are read from right to left

blocks.note: an advert, or commercial on television
a van is a vehicle
eg means for example, as does say
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has a delivery van serviced at the rear of a garage.
explanation.walkthrough: Service reads as a verb to the van, but it is the noun, as in being of service.
explanation.definitionFit: To be of service is to be of benefit or use, which is what advantage means.

clue.text: For this reason ring off once man goes ahead

indicators.note: a ring taken off means the round letter is removed from the word
going ahead places the pronoun at the front of the remaining letters

blocks.note: he is the pronoun for a man
O is round like a ring
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man takes off a wedding ring, explaining why he went ahead once.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring is the round letter, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Hence is a formal adverb meaning therefore, as a consequence, for that cause.

clue.text: Moving towards former president of Egypt

blocks.note: moving in the sense of touching or sorrowful
at can mean in the direction of, as in throw at

explanation.surface: Something advancing on a former Egyptian leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving towards' reads as one phrase of motion; it splits into an adjective and a preposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Anwar Sadat was Egypt's head of state from 1970 until his assassination in 1981.

clue.text: One cuts a fine figure in the garden!

definitions.text: One cuts a fine figure in the garden!

blocks.clueFragment: One cuts a fine figure in the garden!
blocks.note: surface reading: someone looking smart and elegant out among the flowers
setter's reading: a gardener who literally clips hedges into shapes such as birds and animals

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom about looking stylish is taken literally: the person shears bushes into figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Topiary is the art of clipping shrubs into ornamental shapes, and its practitioner sculpts those.

clue.text: Fifty-one scolded and set free

blocks.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
to berate is to scold

explanation.surface: Fifty-one prisoners are given a dressing-down and then released.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberated is a past participle meaning released, emancipated or freed from captivity.

clue.text: Heater once used by people approaching retirement

definitions.text: Heater once used by people approaching retirement

blocks.note: surface reading: older workers nearing the end of their careers
setter's reading: retiring for the night, going to bed, with an old warming pan for the sheets

explanation.walkthrough: Retirement here means turning in for the night, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a long-handled pan of hot coals passed between sheets to take off the chill.

clue.text: Sheltered, as a Parisian once asked

blocks.note: un is French for a
ex means former, once
to pose a question is to ask it

explanation.surface: A Parisian once asked for shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Parisian' is the French indefinite article, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept unexposed is protected from wind, sun or view, that is shielded.

clue.text: Arrogant person raises bitter

blocks.note: to up something is to raise it
tart and bitter are both sharp tastes

explanation.surface: A conceited man orders more pints of bitter beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British pale beer, which steers you toward the pub, but here it is the taste.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone newly risen in status who behaves presumptuously or self-importantly.

clue.text: Flightless bird has flying teal to compete with

indicators.note: a duck in flight is all over the place, so its letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the emu is a flightless Australian bird
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grounded bird tries to keep up with a duck in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: The flightless and flying birds make a neat contrast in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate is to try to match or rival someone, striving to equal them.

clue.text: Half expect to get the Spanish drum out

indicators.note: half of a word keeps only its first part, here three letters of six

blocks.note: the first half of the word
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Someone half expects a Spanish drummer to be thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: To drum someone out is to dismiss them in disgrace, to throw out or banish them.

clue.text: Complain and drag bunk inside

indicators.note: inside puts the nonsense word within the nuisance word

blocks.note: a drag is a bore or nuisance, a pest
bunk and rot both mean nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles and hauls a bunk bed indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: P(ROT)EST: drag and bunk are nouns, not a verb and a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest is to object or raise a grievance, which is to complain.

clue.text: Understatement gives false impression about child

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the falsehoods go round the youngster

blocks.note: to lie is to give a false impression
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: Playing things down misleads people about a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: LI(TOT)ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is a figure of speech that affirms by negating the opposite, as in 'not bad'.

clue.text: Peacekeeping force in South Africa, a hot place

blocks.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
the United Nations sends peacekeeping forces
taken as written

explanation.surface: UN troops deployed to a sweltering spot in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Peacekeeping force points to the United Nations, whose blue-helmeted troops keep the peace.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauna is a steam or dry-heat room, literally a very warm spot to sit in.

clue.text: Fall guy gapes, with coat ruined

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and remade

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hapless man stares open-mouthed at his spoiled coat, the butt of the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall guy is someone made to take the blame for others, which is a scapegoat.

clue.text: Screen is erected the day before

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected means stood up, so the word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
the eve is the day before an event

explanation.surface: A screen goes up the day before a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen is to filter or sift, and a sieve is a mesh for straining or sifting.

clue.text: Call for cut rejected by court

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word reads in reverse

blocks.note: to axe is to cut
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Demands for spending cuts are thrown out by the court.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to demand and obtain something, such as payment or obedience.

clue.text: Greed is a weakness, a redhead admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so these letters go inside the failing

blocks.note: taken as written
a vice is a moral failing
taken as written
the head, or first letter, of the colour

explanation.surface: A red-haired person confesses that greed is their failing.
explanation.walkthrough: A, then VICE with A and R let in: A V(AR)ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an excessive desire for wealth or gain, a synonym for greed.

clue.text: Most miserly change to means test? No way!

indicators.note: saying no to the road means removing its abbreviation from the phrase

blocks.note: a check on income before benefits are paid
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: Someone protests at a stingy reform of the means test.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking ST out of the middle of MEANSTEST leaves the answer. A means test assesses a person's income to decide eligibility for state benefits.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean is miserly, so the superlative meanest describes whoever is stingiest of all.

clue.text: One of those offering support to the board?

definitions.text: One of those offering support to the board?

blocks.clueFragment: One of those offering support to the board?
blocks.note: surface reading: a loyal backer of the company directors
setter's reading: a flat plank of wood held up from beneath, like a table top

explanation.walkthrough: The board sounds like a company's directors; it is a literal plank resting on a frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a framework of legs supporting a horizontal plank to make a table.

clue.text: Turns to go off at quarter to six, nine short

indicators.note: short of nine means the Roman nine is taken away from the number word

blocks.note: food that goes off rots
taken as written
east is a compass quarter
taken as written
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone leaves at a quarter to six, nine people missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarter to six' looks like a time; quarter is a compass point, and SIX loses IX to leave S.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotates and turns are both verbs for spinning or revolving about an axis.
